newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan president opens oilfield in country's south.
newsitem.headline: Sudan president opens oilfield in country's south.

text.p: Sudan's President Lt-General Omar Hassan al-Bashir on Monday opened an oilfield in southern Sudan that was developed with Qatari partnership.
State radio said the opening of Adar Yar field in Upper Nile state marked "the start of actual production and commercial exploitation of petroleum from the three wells in the area."
Initial output in the field, about 600 km (375 miles) south of Khartoum, is 5,000 barrels per day and could rise, it said.
The radio said the president also inaugurated facilities to transport the petroleum to an area where it would be transported by trucks to the port at Melut, the main town in the province.
It said the digging of the wells and their maintenance was undertaken by Qatar Petroleum Company. The production company is the Sudan branch of Gulf Petroleum Company (GPC).
Sudan and Qatar set up the GPC in August 1995, owned by the Qatar Petroleum Company (60 percent), and the two Sudanese firms Concorp and National Petroleum Company with 20 percent each.
The field was discovered in the 1980s but insecurity and lack of finance were reported to have delayed its development.
